subject: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & next steps (token volumes)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & next steps (token volumes)

Thanks for taking the time today — really appreciate the clear demo and context on how Acme is planning to route user queries. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can produce a clean invoice estimate and cost model: 

TL;DR: Attached is a first-pass pricing workbook and a simple token-cost CSV. Can you confirm the expected monthly token volumes (approx):
- Ingest/embedding tokens (batch): ~____ tokens/month
- Generation tokens (chat/assistant): ~____ tokens/month
- Peak qps and 95th percentile latency SLOs (if you have them)

Specific asks: 
1) Volume ranges: best guess min / expected / max for generation tokens per month (we'll model unit economics for 1M-token blocks).
2) Target budget range or target $ per 1M tokens you want us to hit (e.g., $X / 1M tokens).
3) Any procurement constraints (PO required, invoice cadence monthly vs quarterly).

What I attached:
- ACME-Redwood-pricing-v1.xlsx — line-item estimate with hosted API vs dedicated pool scenarios.
- token-cost-breakdown.csv — simple per-1M-token math and assumptions (compute, storage, KV cache hit-rate).
- redwood-invoice-estimate-ACME.pdf — one-page summary (PDF).

High-level notes on assumptions in this draft: 
- Baseline hosted API rate (on curated open model): $18 / 1M generation tokens (example) — this includes model execution and ephemeral KV/cache benefits.
- Reserved/dedicated discount applied at commit tiers: 25% off for 3-month commit, 40% for 12-month commit (illustrative).
- Caching and prefix reuse assumed to reduce billable generation tokens by ~15% for your UI flows.

Next steps: if you can reply with the volume ranges and whether procurement needs a SOW + PO, I'll finalize a scoped invoice and send a short one-page justification for billing to share with your finance team. Happy to hop on a 30-minute follow-up Monday if helpful.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: ACME-Redwood-pricing-v1.xlsx, token-cost-breakdown.csv, redwood-invoice-estimate-ACME.pdf

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>, Carlos Mendoza <carlos.mendoza@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & next steps (token volumes)

Thanks Sean — good recap. A few quick answers from our side: 
- Best-guess monthly generation tokens (current pilot): min 10M / expected 35M / max 120M.
- Embedding/batch offline tokens: ~2M tokens/month.
- Target cost: we'd like to keep hosted spend around $1,200 - $1,800 / month initially, but we can expand if the unit economics make sense (targeting <$50 per 1M tokens effective).
- Procurement: we do require a standard PO for any purchase > $5k and a 30-day net invoice cadence.

Couple follow-ups: can you show both hosted pricing and a dedicated committed option at the 12-month level? Also want to see how caching assumptions change the effective $/1M.

Happy to take the Monday call — Priya, Carlos, and I can make room in the morning.

-Jordan
Director of Product
Acme Corp
jordan.lee@acme.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>

Date: Sat, 16 Jan 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & next steps (token volumes)

Jordan — great, thanks for the numbers. I updated the attached workbook with two scenarios (hosted API and dedicated 12-mo commit) using your volume bands and a conservative cache benefit. Summary bullets below (numbers are illustrative and fully itemized in the workbook):

Summary (generation tokens only):
- Pilot band (~10M / month): Hosted estimate = $180 / month (note: this is the compute charge from model execution only) — effective $/1M = $18.
- Expected band (~35M / month): Hosted estimate = $630 / month — effective $/1M = $18.
- Max band (~120M / month): Hosted estimate = $1,980 / month (we apply volume discounts starting at 50M) — effective $/1M = $16.5.

Dedicated 12-mo commit (reserved GPU pool) — amortized cost per 1M tokens assumes 60% utilization and includes ops/support:
- Expected band (~35M): Effective $/1M = $11 (after 12-mo 40% discount + caching). Total monthly commit ~$385.
- Max band (~120M): Effective $/1M = $9.50 (higher utilization).

Caching assumptions applied in model: prefix reuse + short-term KV cache hit-rate of 20% (your flows showed repeated prompts), which reduces billable generation tokens by ~20% in the model; we include a sensitivity tab (10%/20%/30%).

Invoice/what's included: unit compute for model execution, KV/cache ops, storage for session state < 30 days, standard support. Additional items (chargeable) — encryption key management (BYO KMS), extended retention, and premium SLAs are listed separately in the workbook.

I attached a one-page invoice-style PDF you can share with procurement that maps to the hosted vs dedicated options. If Acme is targeting <$50 per 1M tokens, you're easily within that range in all scenarios — we show $9.5–$18 / 1M depending on commitment and utilization.

Proposed next steps: 
- You confirm which scenario (hosted vs dedicated) you prefer for the pilot so we can lock assumptions.
- I'll send a formal quote and a draft MSA + SOW if you want to move to a committed deal.
- Let's lock a 30-min call Monday 9:00–9:30 PT to review the workbook with Priya and Carlos.

If those times work, Marissa (copied) will send the invite and include the workbook link.

Thanks,
Sean
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference

Attachments: ACME-Redwood-pricing-v1.xlsx, token-cost-breakdown.csv, redwood-invoice-estimate-ACME.pdf
